name: The widow and her two mites
charge: Casting in all that she had, even all her living
summary: He sat over against the treasury and watched the rich cast in much. A poor widow threw in two mites, which make a farthing. He called his disciples to see it, and weighed it against everything else in the box: she had cast in more than they all.
offense: And there came a certain poor widow, and she threw in two mites, which make a farthing. The rich cast in of their abundance; she of her want did cast in all that she had, even all her living. No one had asked her for it.
judgment: And he called unto him his disciples, and saith unto them, Verily I say unto you, That this poor widow hath cast more in, than all they which have cast into the treasury: for all they did cast in of their abundance; but she of her want did cast in all that she had, even all her living. Her gift is the standard by which every other gift in the temple that day was found smaller, and it is read in every generation since.

entries.commentary: The vineyard is let out to husbandmen who beat and kill the servants sent for the fruit, and at last kill the son to seize the inheritance. The vineyard is the nation; the servants are the prophets, who were beaten, stoned and killed, and who all came with the same message. Then the son came with that message and they killed him too. The stone which the builders rejected is become the head of the corner. They knew he had spoken the parable against them.

The Pharisees and Herodians come with flattery first: we know that thou art true, and carest for no man. Then comes the trap about tribute to Caesar. That is still how men come to this word. They will say they like what is being said and then set the thing they disagree with beside it. Knowing their hypocrisy, he calls for the penny and answers by the image on it: Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's. They were careful of Caesar's law while mishandling the priesthood.

The Sadducees bring the seven brethren and one wife, and are answered, Ye therefore do greatly err, because ye know not the scriptures, neither the power of God. The law they built the question on was for inheritance, so that a dead man's name and portion would not be put out of Israel. When they shall rise from the dead, they neither marry, nor are given in marriage. A woman is bound by that law while her husband lives, and in the resurrection there is no more dying. He is not the God of the dead, but the God of the living.

The first of all the commandments is, Hear, O Israel; The Lord our God is one Lord: and thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart. The second is, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. There is none other commandment greater than these. Loving him is keeping his commandments, and loving your neighbour as yourself means holding him to them as you hold yourself, because the wages of sin is death and you do not want to see your brother die. The scribe answered discreetly, and was told, Thou art not far from the kingdom of God, and no man after that durst ask him any question.

How say the scribes that Christ is the son of David? David himself said by the Holy Ghost, The Lord said to my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand. Beware of the scribes, which love to go in long clothing, and love salutations in the marketplaces, and the chief seats in the synagogues. What they wanted was the recognition of men.
The rich cast in much, but the poor widow threw in two mites, and he says she cast in more than they all, for they cast in of their abundance, but she of her want did cast in all that she had.

Observe the month of Abib and keep the passover unto the Most High, for in the month of Abib the Lord thy God brought thee forth out of Egypt by night. Thou shalt eat no leavened bread with it; seven days shalt thou eat unleavened bread, even the bread of affliction, because thou camest forth out of the land of Egypt in haste, that thou mayest remember the day all the days of thy life. Nothing of the flesh sacrificed the first day at even, the lamb, may remain all night until the morning. The passover may not be sacrificed within any of thy gates, but only at the place which the Lord thy God shall choose to place his name there, at even, at the going down of the sun. Six days thou shalt eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day is a solemn assembly and no work: the first day of the passover is a sabbath, and the seventh day of the passover is a sabbath.

Seven weeks shalt thou number unto thee: begin to number the seven weeks from such time as thou beginnest to put the sickle to the corn, and keep the feast of weeks unto the Most High with a tribute of a freewill offering according as the Lord thy God hath blessed thee. Another name for the feast of weeks is the feast of firstfruits: you count seven weeks and then a day, fifty days, which is Pentecost. Rejoice before the Most High, thou and thy son and thy daughter, thy manservant and thy maidservant, the Levite, the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow; and remember that thou wast a bondman in Egypt.

Thou shalt observe the feast of tabernacles seven days, after that thou hast gathered in thy corn and thy wine. Rejoice in thy feast, thou and thy son and thy daughter, thy manservant and thy maidservant, the Levite, the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow within thy gates. Seven days shalt thou keep a solemn feast in the place which the Lord shall choose, because the Most High shall bless thee in all thine increase and in all the works of thine hands; therefore thou shalt surely rejoice.

Three times in a year shall all thy males appear before the Most High in the place which he shall choose: in the feast of unleavened bread, in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of tabernacles. They shall not appear before the Lord empty, meaning they have to come with their sacrifices: every man shall give as he is able, according to the blessing of the Lord thy God which he hath given thee.

Judges and officers shalt thou make thee in all thy gates, throughout thy tribes, and they shall judge the people with just judgment. There is nothing new under the sun: when you see judges and officers among us today, know that we are following the things that are written within this book. Thou shalt not wrest judgment, thou shalt not respect persons, neither take a gift, for a gift doth blind the eyes of the wise and pervert the words of the righteous. That which is altogether just shalt thou follow, that thou mayest live and inherit the land.

Thou shalt not plant thee a grove of any trees near unto the altar of the Lord thy God; yet these pastors set up Christmas trees inside the church, directly against this law. Neither shalt thou set thee up any image, which the Lord thy God hateth.

verses.text: And Jesus sat over against the treasury, and beheld how the people cast money into the treasury: and many that were rich cast in much.
And there came a certain poor widow, and she threw in two mites, which make a farthing.
And he called unto him his disciples, and saith unto them, Verily I say unto you, That this poor widow hath cast more in, than all they which have cast into the treasury:
For all they did cast in of their abundance; but she of her want did cast in all that she had, even all her living.
And he looked up, and saw the rich men casting their gifts into the treasury.
And he saw also a certain poor widow casting in thither two mites.
And he said, Of a truth I say unto you, that this poor widow hath cast in more than they all:
For all these have of their abundance cast in unto the offerings of God: but she of her penury hath cast in all the living that she had.
For if there be first a willing mind, it is accepted according to that a man hath, and not according to that he hath not.
Every man shall give as he is able, according to the blessing of the Lord thy God which he hath given thee.
If thou hast abundance give alms accordingly: if thou have but a little, be not afraid to give according to that little:
